title: Integrated Imputation-Classification for Supervised Learning with Missing Data
claim: A generator completes missing inputs and a single classification loss trains both generator and discriminator end to end.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, feedback loop underneath, skip connection over top
description: A single-row block diagram flowing left to right. At the far left is the input, the bold math pair (x̃, m), labeled in gray as an incomplete data sample with its missing mask. A thick arrow leads into a large box labeled Generator. A noise vector z enters the Generator from above, labeled as a random noise sample. A long skip line from the input goes over the top and down into a circled-plus node. The Generator output also feeds this node. The node outputs x̂, labeled as the imputed data sample, into a box labeled Multi-class Discriminator on the right. A return arrow runs from the Discriminator along the bottom, labeled Classification loss, and points back up into the Generator. The figure is black and white with gray annotations. The eye goes first to the two large boxes.
caption: Schematic of the IICN network. The completed sample ˆx is made up of the output of the generator and the observed parts of an incomplete sample ˜x. The completed sample ˆx is passed to a multi-class discriminator. The classification loss is applied to update both the generator and the discriminator.
abstract: We study supervised classification problems with missing feature values. Existing approaches often decouple imputation from classification, producing imputations that may be plausible but uninformative for prediction. Instead, we propose the Integrated Imputation and Classification Network (IICN), which jointly trains an imputer and an ${(n{+}1)}$-class discriminator adversarially with a single class-supervised objective, where the discriminator learns to distinguish among the $n$ true classes and an additional ``imputed'' class. We prove that it admits a global optimum where the imputer and discriminator together implement marginalization over missing coordinates and yield a Bayes-optimal classifier. We evaluate IICN on FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and tabular datasets with naturally occurring missingness. IICN outperforms classical impute-then-classify pipelines and recent generative baselines, showing strong robustness and accuracy in challenging settings.
